events.title: Emergence
events.description:
Emergence will be on exhibit from November 17th – January 10th, with the opening reception on Wednesday, November 18th! 
A flock of birds, a forest ecosystem, a language, or a community cannot be fully explained by studying a single component in isolation. Approaching questions of identity, ecology, memory, labor, and transformation from a distinct perspective, this group of artists examine personal narrative through craft practices tied to exploration of that narrative. Their works create an ecosystem of ideas in which individual voices remain while contributing to a larger meditation on our…

events.description:
UrbanSparkle is the annual UrbanGlass feature of jewelry utilizing glass, in tandem with NYC Jewelry Week. This year’s selection brings together metal and glass techniques by highlighting four artists utilizing enamel in their wearable work. The exhibition is available from November 17th – January 1oth, with the opening reception on Wednesday, November 18th!

events.description:
Join Haiti Cultural Exchange on Thursday nights for the second edition of the Mizik Ayiti! Residency Series. The Late Fall residency will be held by Bonga Jean Baptiste & Sanba Kebyesou. 
Heralded for their skill as musicians, educators, and culture bearers, Bonga and Kebyesou Danlè maintain the power of Haitian culture held in the tanbou. With a wide-ranging repertoire of Haitian traditional rhythms, they have revitalized the rasin mizik movement through their many years on stage.

events.title: Immigrant Nation: Making Home in Song and Story
events.description:
From Victrolas to tapes to TikTok, in clubs and record stores, through changing attitudes to immigration, people have used sound to express the trials and sorrows, hopes and humor of risking the journey to a new life. 
Join us for an evening of discussion and archival music recordings as David Goren and Maria Margaronis explore how immigrants to America have used songs, skits, and recorded messages from the founding of Ellis Island to the present day in order to connect with home, to find their way, and to feel less alone.

events.description:
ISSUE Project Room celebrates the 20th Anniversary of its Artists-In-Residence (AIR) program throughout 2026 with performances by current residents and returning alumni. This anniversary season highlights AIRs whose work reflects the ongoing evolution of a much broader community of experimental artists who have helped shape ISSUE for over twenty years.

events.title: Broken Dishes Book Club with Swati
events.description:
Have you ever watched a woman blow up her life, and thought, good for her? This is a book club for those who seek to disrupt notions of domestic bliss – we want batshit plots, women who don’t settle, and eleventh hour plot twists. We want all this packaged into a very literary 300 pages or less. This book club will explore should-be and to-be classics by literary hotties of centuries past. Leave the dirty dishes at home and come indulge with us.

events.title: NYCJW x UrbanGlass: Handcrafted in Flame
events.description: UrbanGlass is partnering with NYC Jewelry Week to present a day of hands-on experiences and live demonstrations celebrating the artistry behind handmade jewelry. Taking place on Saturday, November 21, the event invites participants to explore how everyday adornment is created—from molten glass to finished piece. Visitors can join 45-minute beadmaking sessions in the flame shop (ages 14+) and jewelry construction workshops in the classroom (ages 10+), each offering a step-by-step look at the techniques, tools, and decisions that shape handcrafted work. Ongoing live demos throughout the day…

events.title: Storytelling: Nurturing the Field at NYC Jewelry Week 2026
events.description:
Connecting libraries, books, and archives to strengthen knowledge sharing and community in jewelry.


What do a book series, a community library, and a magazine archive have in common? (Hint: it is a lot more than words printed on paper.)  
Join BPL for an informative and engaging conversation on the resource sharing, community connectivity, and collaborations essential to projects by Karen Davidov (founder, The Jewelry Library), Iris Eichenberg & Jimena Ríos (co-authors, Still/ Todavía and This sketchbook belongs to /Este cuaderno pertenece a), and Adriane Dalton (editor, Metalsmith).

events.title: Knit Together
events.description:
Join BPL to spend quality time working on knitting or crochet projects, getting inspired, and building friendships with fellow fiber enthusiasts. All skill levels are welcome, and we’ll help you cast on and knit your first stitches if you’re looking to learn! 
Knitting is a relaxing, mindful activity that helps reduce stress while giving your hands something creative to focus on. Come work on your projects, share tips and inspiration, and connect with others as we build community through a shared love of yarn.

events.title: Fraction, Refraction: Artist Talk
events.description:
This program brings together Kerr Cirilo, Clare Hu, and Basharat Ali Syed to discuss their encounters with images of national significance on the occasion of the exhibition Fraction, Refraction. 
Fraction, Refraction brings together image-based works that push and pull highlighted, forgotten, or obscured layers of history to offer entry points into its constructed truths. Refraction is a scientific process whereby a wave bends as it passes through at least two mediums of differing densities, altering the wave’s speed and direction. events.title: Literary Black Book Club with Genay
events.description:
The Literary Black Book Club will meet every month to discuss mostly contemporary fiction written by Black authors.  We’ll also share a light snack and hopefully some laughs. 
This month we’ll discuss Nafissa Thompson Spires’ sly, spry, literary debut novel about the murder of an infamous moonshiner and the cacophony of true stories a small town can tell about itself, The Four Wives and Five Deaths of Richard Milford.

events.title: RestFest Film Festival
events.description:
RestFest Film Festival is an artist-run virtual film and video art festival & online gathering space created by and for the Crip, Disabled, Deaf, Chronically ill, Neurodivergent, and Mad community. 
This December, RestFest is partnering with the Brooklyn Public Library to present seven films and video artworks from their 2024 and 2026 festival programs. With these films, you will find a wide range of topics, genres, and forms. RestFest promotes free creative expression from all Disabled artists, embracing the community’s artistry and diverse voices without the restrictions of only creating…

events.title: The First Novel Fête
events.description:
Join the Center for Fiction for the best book(ish) party in Brooklyn. The First Novel Fête is one of our favorite traditions, celebrating the seven debut novelists shortlisted for our First Novel Prize. Enjoy readings from the finalists’ work, meet and mingle with some of today’s most celebrated writers, catch up over light bites and drinks from our open bar, win door prizes from our generous sponsors, and more. This year’s Fête once again promises to be a fun, festive evening—we can’t wait to see you there. 
The Fête also helps sustain our work for readers and writers of all ages. Proceeds…

events.title: Crocheting Workshop
events.description:
Learn, Create and Enjoy a New Hobby! 
Come and join the Library for Arts & Culture for a fun and creative crocheting workshop!  In this hands-on workshop you will have the opportunity to learn the basics of crocheting, improve your skills, ask questions, get helpful tips from Maggie and meet other people who enjoy crafting. 
Join Maggie Koluch, a Polish artisan who has worked with designers across New York’s fashion industry. Crochet, knitting, and handcraft are skills she developed long before she applied them professionally. 
Today, Maggie collaborates with designers across New York’s…

events.title: Disintegration 33 1/3: Andi Harriman in Conversation with Leila Taylor
events.description:
In 1989, The Cure’s Robert Smith was going to turn thirty years old. His fears and anxieties of age-having not yet written his pinnacle album-caused Smith to embark on the band’s undoing with Disintegration. The result was an LP drenched in melancholy sublime, a beautiful decree of breaking down to build anew. From the fame and notoriety of The Cure after their hit, “Just Like Heaven,” to the departure of the only other consistent band member, Lol Tolhurst, it’s clear that the grisly spiral into the depths of pain is stamped throughout Disintegration. 
Join author Andi Harriman, in…

events.title: Short(er) Slavic Novels Book Club with Arya
events.description: Are you intimidated by the great (and by great, we mean looooooong) novels of Dostoevsky or Tolstoy, Ulitskaya and Tokarczuk? Novels over 500 pages may not be a crime to read, but they can, at times, feel like a punishment to finish. That’s why we’re is introducing SHORT(ER) SLAVIC NOVELS, a book club dedicated to Russian, Ukrainian, Polish, Belarusian, Czech, etc. novels under 300 pages. All titles will be read in English, so previous knowledge of Slavic languages is NOT required. (Uk)Rain(e) or shine, czech out our Downtown Brooklyn location every month for classic and contemporary Slavic…

events.title: Reading for the Craft Book Club with Pedro & Swati
events.description: Writing is an “apprenticeship to what can never fully be mastered”, says the Pulitzer-winning poet Carl Phillips. Join us as we delve into the mysteries of the art of storytelling. In this workshop-adjacent book club, we will discuss everything from plot beats to perspective choices to sentence-level sonics of major literary works and small press gems, in an attempt to understand how specific authorial choices shape the experience and impact of a story. You do not have to be a writer to join us — just someone with a deep love for literature and endless curiosity about how a story gets told.…
